🔍 Reading skill 1: Scanning 扫读定位

In the exam, you will need to find specific information quickly. You should read the question carefully to find out what information it requires, and then find the answer by scanning the reading passage.

Skills builder
  • Move your eyes quickly down the page.
  • Locate the section or sentence that contains the specific information you need. Make use of headings and subheadings to narrow your search.
  • Identify keywords and key phrases in the text to get the correct answer.
💡 Look at the following exampleWhat types of obstacles will students face in the race? → climbing walls and crawling tunnels

You will need to identify obstacles in the race. Types indicates that there will be more than one. Types, obstacles and race are the keywords.

A1 · Read the calendar entries. Then scan the leaflet and complete the entries.

A fun, new race for all!

§1
The Running Club's first-ever obstacle course race is taking place on the school's sports field at 10 a.m. this Saturday. Have you ever taken part in this type of race before? If not, you should definitely give it a go.
§2
Obstacle course races are more fun than normal races because they're unconventional. Instead of just running, you also have to get over or through various challenging obstacles. Saturday's course, with its climbing walls and crawling tunnels, will surely look intimidating. With enough motivation and determination though, anyone can complete it. Sign up for the race in Room 301 by 4 p.m. on Thursday afternoon.

🔑 StrategyDo not read every word when you scan through a text.
A2 · Read the questions below. Then scan the article excerpt and answer the questions.

Unconventional races—past and present

§1
Unconventional races have become a craze in Hong Kong. Their appeal is increasing because they make racing more fun and interesting. Also, many of these competitions are for good causes. Here are two examples:

Sedan Chair Race

§2
The Sedan Chair Race was organized by Sedan Chair Charities Fund between 1975 and 2017. So it had been around for many years before unconventional races became a trend. Teams of four to eight runners raced for various charities while carrying a sedan chair as they raced around The Peak. The course was around two kilometres long, and it brought lots of laughs as teams often dressed up in costumes, and ran the race as firefighters, mad scientists, cats, cartoon characters or witches. Fittingly, the event usually took place around Halloween.

Central Rat Race

§3
This is another event where the competitors often wear unusual clothing. The teams are usually made up of businesspeople and some of them race around in Central in their suits! The race consists of eight obstacles. When a competitor completes an obstacle, he or she must pass a briefcase to a teammate. Only then can the team's next racing stage begin. First held in 2006, the Rat Race helps raise money for MINDSET. This charity helps people with mental health problems.

🔁 Reading skill 2: Recognizing paraphrasing 识别改写

Paraphrasing means using different words to express what someone has said or written. Paraphrasing often employs synonyms—words that have the same or similar meaning as the words they are replacing. It is important to develop your ability to recognize paraphrasing because the wordings of the exam questions are often different from the wordings in the reading passage.

Skills builder
  • Read the question carefully. If the question provides multiple-choice options, read those carefully as well.
  • Identify keywords and key phrases that might help you zero in on the information you need to find in the reading passage.
  • Scan the reading passage. If you cannot find the keywords you identified, then look for synonyms and paraphrases.
B1 · Read the question and underline the keyword(s) and key phrase(s). Then read the article and underline the paraphrases. Finally, answer the question.
In order to become proficient at e-sports, professional gamers must …
Aspecialize in a game they like.
Bapproach gaming seriously as their occupation.
Cget a sponsorship with a well-known company.
Dplay e-sports alongside sports like badminton.

A beginner's guide to e-sports

§1
When you think of sports, you probably think of things like basketball, football and badminton. E-sports, however, don't require a ball or court—instead, the equipment includes big screens and games consoles.
§2
Recently, large-scale competitions have sprung up across the globe, pitting individuals and teams against each other while spectators watch in person and online. Much like professional sports players, the best e-sports players can now earn a good living by winning game tournaments and netting lucrative sponsorships with big-name brands. One of the latest e-sports championships, where gamers battled head-to-head in an arena, drew over 35 million in-person and online viewers.
§3
In order to develop their skills, career gamers must treat playing their favourite games as if it is a full-time job.
B2 · Read the five points on the note sheet. They are paraphrases of some of the sentences in the article. Read the article and underline those sentences.

The only way out is teamwork!

§1
Last Thursday, our school gymnasium underwent a makeover. Instead of discovering the usual squeaky floors and fluorescent lighting, Ms Hong's and Ms Hanover's mathematics classes found quickly but expertly constructed 'escape rooms'! In groups of six, students were required to work together to solve logic problems, maths challenges and a surprise secret ending. Room 1 was pirate-themed; Room 2 resembled a private eye's office, Room 3 made students feel as if they were in a submarine at the bottom of the ocean. Students arrived at 8.30 a.m. and participated in games until 2.30 p.m.
§2
Each team was given a maximum of 20 minutes to escape from their room. About two-thirds of teams managed to escape within the time frame. The winning team from each room received gift vouchers to the school cafeteria.
§3
Darcy Zhang says the game was fun, but she didn't anticipate how tough it would be. 'Not to brag, but I'm usually good at maths,' she says. 'However, being stuck in a small space made it harder for me to think.' Zhang's team placed third in the submarine room, escaping in 12 minutes and 27 seconds.
§4
The top team for Room 1, led by Tommy Chung, finished in 7 minutes and 45 seconds; the top team for Room 2, led by Annie Collingwood, finished in 8 minutes and 12 seconds, and the top team for Room 3, led by Jim Pruitt, finished in 9 minutes and 56 seconds.

Paraphrase points（点击显示对应原文句）

1. The school gym was remodelled.
＿＿＿＿＿
2. Teams needed to work collaboratively to find solutions.
＿＿＿＿＿
3. Teams had no more than 20 minutes to exit the escape rooms.
＿＿＿＿＿
4. The victors won prizes of food from the school.
＿＿＿＿＿
5. Darcy Zhang didn't expect the game to be so challenging.
＿＿＿＿＿

🏊 Exam practice Part A Triathlete trades studies for training
📖 Read Text 1Read Text 1 and answer questions 1–18 on pages 100–102. Sybil Lee leaves her studies at the City University of Hong Kong to pursue her dreams of becoming a world-class athlete. By Andrew Keats

Text 1: Triathlete trades studies for training

Sybil Lee leaves her studies at the City University of Hong Kong to pursue her dreams of becoming a world-class athlete.

By Andrew Keats · 全文 19 段 · 右侧/下方逐段呈现（§1–§19）。

Text 1: Triathlete trades studies for training（§1–§10）
§1
Twenty-year-old professional triathlete Sybil Lee has announced she has left university to concentrate on her training. At a recent press conference, Lee told reporters she was sitting in the fifth row of a psychology lecture when she had an epiphany. 'I realized I needed to quit school,' she said. Lee, who'd just begun her third year at the City University of Hong Kong, had recently placed third in a triathlon held in the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia, Canada.
§2
'My lecturer was talking about the prevalence of mood disorders,' said Lee, 'but all I could think about was my afternoon training session. And lunch.' Lee laughed.
§3
'I have been falling asleep in class,' she continued. 'Swimming lengths in the pool every morning, I suddenly remember a piece of homework I need to finish. It's been stressful.'
§4
Lee, who first attempted a triathlon with her father when she was 15, has slowly turned more of her focus towards the sport. Just before she began her university studies, she landed her first sponsorship deal.
§5
'I stayed in school initially because I didn't realize I had any other options,' said Lee. 'I had worked so hard to get into university.'
§6
Over the past year, however, her two passions—school and training—have begun to clash.
§7
'I've become stronger and stronger in my sport,' Lee said, 'and weaker and weaker in school.'
§8
'Most people talk about the value of a good education. Some people have the motivation and determination to excel at both school and sport. I think I'm just the type of person who needs to focus on one thing at a time.'
§9
Lee, who has steadily been offered more sponsorship deals as she improves as a triathlete, now earns her living through her sport.
§10
'One of the most challenging obstacles for young athletes is figuring out how they can afford to follow their passion,' Lee told reporters. 'I am lucky enough to have the financial support to do so.'
Text 1: Triathlete trades studies for training（§11–§19）
§11
Lee left that psychology lecture during a break two weeks ago, and immediately went to the school's administration to apply for a leave from her studies.
§12
'I spoke to my father,' she says. 'He was supportive. "This is an unconventional choice, but I believe it is the best choice for you," he said.'
§13
Lee has competitions coming up in Hawaii, Japan and France. By setting academics aside, she will be able to train daily, and place more emphasis on diet and psychological preparation.
§14
'The triathlon consists of swimming, cycling and running,' says Lee. 'Running and cycling have always held an appeal for me. Swimming is my weakest area. I'll now be able to take more time to swim outside, in cold water, in preparation for open-water swims.'
§15
Now that Lee is no longer a student, she has turned her studious nature towards studying the history of her sport. The first documented triathlon was held outside Paris, France, in the 1920s, and consisted of a 3-kilometre run, a 12-kilometre bike ride, and a swim across the channel Marne. The first endurance triathlon, which combined a marathon-length run with a 3.9-kilometre swim and a 180-kilometre bike race, took place in Hawaii in 1978. The first-ever Ironman triathlon, the Hawaii endurance triathlon grew out of an argument between runners, swimmers and cyclists as to who was the most athletic. The 1978 race was won by Gordon Haller, a Navy communications specialist.
§16
Though Lee races the Olympic-length triathlon, which consists of a 1.5-kilometre swim, 40-kilometre bike race and 10-kilometre run, she is excited to compete in Hawaii, the home of the Ironman. 'I've never competed in that event, but it is an eventual goal of mine,' she says. 'I feel like I'll be visiting a little piece of history.'
§17
Reflecting on leaving university, Lee has some words of wisdom for other student athletes. 'I made the choice that was right for me. I want to be able to compete at the highest level of my sport while I'm young. I want to see how far I can go with it.'
§18
Lee says her father was the one who told her to put her studies on hold for a year, rather than simply dropping out. This gives her the option of a trial year. After a year passes, she may return to her studies. Or, if training is going well, she will continue to focus on her sport.
§19
'I value education,' says Lee. 'Even if I choose not to return in a year, I may still go back to school when I'm older, to pursue my BA in psychology. Schooling is a worthwhile venture, and it teaches you a lot about the world. In my case, training for sports is a type of real-world education I have the luck to get to try out.'
§END
END OF READING PASSAGE

Exam practice · Part B1
Part B1
Read Texts 2–3 and answer questions 19–38.
📄 Text 2

A degree in video gaming?
An interview with e-sports degree holder Fred Jones
By Edith Patterson

✉️ Text 3

Letter to the Editor
By Zach Halberstam

Text 2: A degree in video gaming? · An interview with e-sports degree holder Fred Jones · By Edith Patterson
§1
This year, 24-year-old Fred Jones made history as one of the first people to graduate with a degree in the business of e-sports. We interviewed him to learn more about this unusual degree.
How did you end up studying e-sports?
§2
My parents always encouraged me to spend less time binge-playing Counter-Strike and more time studying. I guess my enthusiasm won out, though! I started off at the University of Ohio studying history, but I took a business course four years ago, in my first year, that had a module on e-sports. I changed my major the next semester. My parents weren't too happy about that.
What exactly is a degree in e-sports? What did you study?
§3
My degree is essentially a business degree that focuses on the new context of e-sports. So we studied how to organize e-sports events, how to create events where amateur and elite players, and sponsors could really come together for mutual benefit, and how to advance e-sports globally. We learnt about marketing, we learnt about pitching to brands, and we learnt about how to choose which players to support to best reach our target markets when it comes to selling games and spreading awareness about competitive e-sports.
Did you get to play video games as part of your degree?
§4
Sometimes! For research. It wasn't a huge component of what we did, but we did get to develop research projects focused on our favourite games, and we did get to try out new video games, sometimes before they hit the market. I got to try out a new adventure game where you play as a dog, a first-person shooter game, Days Gone, a zombie game and an animated card game.
What kind of career options does a degree in e-sports open up for you after graduation?
§5
I did some contract work for some e-sports tournaments while I was in school, and I recently joined a major firm to help them develop their communications and marketing for e-sports competitions. My job allows me to travel and to do work every day that I am passionate about. My parents are proud of me now. I'd recommend pursuing a degree in e-sports.
Text 3: Letter to the Editor
Dear Editor,
§1
As a 60-year-old scientist nearing the end of a long career, I was shocked to read your interview with Fred Jones—in the business section, no less.
§2
I graduated from the University of California, Irvine, in 1985 with a master's in biology. I have spent my career working in labs and applying my knowledge to the betterment of the world. My colleagues and I come to work every day knowing that we make a difference.
§3
Don't get me wrong: studies in the humanities, for example, contribute valuable knowledge to our society in a way that is worthwhile.
§4
But beyond allowing Mr Jones to find a job he enjoyed after graduation, I do not see a reason why universities should be offering business courses in video games. Countries across the world are currently grappling with a rise in rates of obesity and diseases related to diet and lifestyle. Our economies are not doing as well as they were a decade ago.
§5
Our students should be studying topics that will help encourage the betterment of society. Degrees should work in service of our country, making sure all our citizens have access to good education, healthcare and housing, instead of spending excess money on games consoles and the many video games associated with them.
§6
I do not blame Mr Jones for choosing an easy path when it came to his studies. I blame his alma mater, the University of Ohio. I also blame my own alma mater, as the University of California, Irvine in fact started off the trend, launching a League of Legends scholarship programme in 2016.
§7
It is time for this trend to come to a halt. Our universities are meant to be places that advance the public good.
Yours faithfully,
Zach Halberstam
§END
END OF READING PASSAGES

Text 1: Being a pro gamer · Posted by John on 19 September (§1–§5)
§1
A lot of you have been asking me what life is really like for a professional e-sports player like myself, so I thought I'd try to address all those questions in this post. Before I get started, though, I think a pre-emptive apology might be in order. You see, I have a feeling not all of you will be entirely happy with what follows.
§2
But let's start with the positives—because there are plenty of those, don't get me wrong. I've always been an avid gamer, so getting to play video games for a living is in many ways a dream come true. I get paid what most people would consider an absurd amount of money to do something I genuinely love, and as an added bonus, I get to travel the world. So far, my job has taken me to more than a dozen different countries, both for tournaments and various promotional events, and that's certainly well above the average for someone who hasn't yet turned 20.
§3
Not only do I get to travel, but I get to do so in style. As I've climbed in the e-sports world rankings, the level of comfort I enjoy when on the road (or in the air) has increased significantly, to the point where I now get to stay in five-star hotels, dine in great restaurants and fly either business or first class, all on someone else's dime. I'd obviously be lying if I said I didn't enjoy that.
§4
Still, the reality is that there are also downsides to this job, even to the actual gameplay. As I've established myself as a League of Legends player, and make a living from it, that's now literally the only game I ever play. Of course, I love LoL. But you know what they say: variety is the spice of life. I'd love to be able to play a story-driven single-player game once in a while, but after I've logged more than 14 hours of gameplay in a single day just to maintain my LoL skills, I don't exactly feel like playing another game just for fun. And I truly miss that.
§5
All that travelling also takes a toll, along with the other pressures that come with this job. Virtually all pro gamers are contractually obligated to stream online for several hours a day and make themselves almost permanently accessible to the media and fans. Trust me, if you think being a professional e-sports player means living a life of leisure, you're sorely mistaken.
Text 1: Being a pro gamer (§6–§10) + Comments
§6
If any of you out there are dreaming about a career as a pro gamer, keep in mind that the competition in e-sports is no less fierce than it is in other professional sports. Just because you've managed to play through Halo a few times on the Legendary difficulty setting doesn't mean you have what it takes to make it as a professional e-sports competitor.
§7
Even if you do make it, you're highly unlikely to have a long career, as your reflexes will inevitably slow down as you get older. While this is true for pro athletes as well, it's a much bigger issue in pro gaming, where most players compete for no more than one or two years. This is evidenced by the fact that the average age of a Major League Baseball player in the US is almost 30 whereas in the League of Legends Championship Series it's just over 21.
§8
Another area where pro gamers have it worse than pro athletes is job security. Of course, we all worry about having our lucrative contracts terminated, but in pro gaming all it really takes is one poor tournament performance for the owner of the team to drop you like a hot potato and hire someone else.
§9
Added to this is a problem I don't think I'm alone in experiencing among pro gamers. As I've hinted at already, becoming one of the very best players in the world of a particular game means you have to make some serious sacrifices. For me, those sacrifices very much included my studies. Because I spent my teenage years playing League of Legends rather than studying, I simply don't have the qualifications to switch to another lucrative career once my gaming days are over. So yeah, I do worry a bit about my future.
§10
Anyway, there you have it, folks: the ups and downs of being a professional gamer. Let me know your thoughts in the comments!

引入 · 标题对比分析
引入 · Phase 1
哪条更像新闻标题？为什么？
标题 A
It Rained Very Heavily Yesterday
• 过去时（Rained）→ 缺乏即时感
• "Very Heavily" → 模糊修饰
• "Yesterday" → 时间词多余
• 7 个词 → 但信息密度低
标题 B
Storm Closes All Schools Across City
• 现在时（Forces）→ ✅ 即时感强
• "Storm" + "Shutdown" → ✅ 具体关键词
• "City-Wide School" → ✅ 范围明确
• 6 个词 → ✅ 更短但信息更多
标题 A 像口语描述，标题 B 才是新闻标题。一条好的 headline 不是"描述事件"，而是用最少词、最强动词抓住核心信息。

Headline：新闻的"门面"
什么是 Headline？
👆 点击翻牌看定义
Headline（标题）
用最少的词概括新闻的核心内容。
✓ 抓住读者注意力
✓ 传达最关键的信息
✓ 让读者决定是否继续读
📖 教材关键词：essence of the event, captures the reader's attention
讲解 · 好标题铁律 ①②
讲解 · Phase 2
好标题的 4 条 MUST · ① ②
MUST ①：抓住注意力
👆 翻牌看说明
instantly capture attention
• 用强力动词制造画面感
• 激发好奇心
📌 何为强力动词？
本身自带画面和力量感的动词，一个词就能替代「形容词 + 弱动词」的组合。
❌ 形容词 + 弱动词 → ✅ 强力动词
Heavy rain causes shutdown → Storm forces shutdown
Very good result happens → Team storms to victory
28 points help team win → 28 pts fire team to title
💡 强力动词 = 画面 + 动作 + 信息，三合一！
MUST ②：简洁有信息量
👆 翻牌看说明
short, informative & interesting
• 5–10 词为佳
• 去掉无意义修饰
• 每条词都承载信息
📌 标题大写规则（Title Case）
标题中所有实词首字母必须大写！
✅ Student, 15, Beats Adults at Chess
❌ Student, 15, beats Adults at chess
大写：名词/动词/形容词/副词；小写：冠词/连词/短介词（a/the/and/in/of）
但冠词/连词出现在句首时也要大写
讲解 · 好标题铁律 ③④
讲解 · Phase 2
好标题的 4 条 MUST · ③ ④
MUST ③：含关键词
👆 翻牌看说明
contain keywords
• 人名、地名、事件名
• 帮助读者立即定位
• 提高搜索可见度
✅ Dragon Slayers Claim E-sports Title
❌ A Great Tournament Happened
MUST ④：概括全文
👆 翻牌看说明
give a sense of the story
• 读标题知大意
• 不误导读者
• 标题即摘要
✅ Chan's 28 Points Lead Team to Basketball Title
❌ Something Happened at a Game

关键提醒：时态与标点
最重要的两点是什么？
👆 点击翻牌
必须做到 vs 建议做到
🔴 必须做到（MUST）：
1. 抓住注意力 (capture attention)
2. 简洁 + 有信息 (short & informative)

🟡 建议做到（MAY）：

3. 逗号代替 and · 4. 无句号结尾

Section 1：Headlines 标题识别 (16分)
独立完成以下题目
📝 Section 1A：选择最佳标题（8分 · 4题）
Q1. 一篇关于本校机器人队赢得全港比赛金牌的报道。
A. A Very Great Science Competition Was Held Last Week
B. Robotics Team Wins Gold at City Science Contest
C. The Robotics Team Has Won a Gold Medal at the City Contest
B现在时 Wins ✅、含关键词 Robotics/Gold、简洁 7 词。A 弱修饰+过去时；C 太长（Has Won 过去时）。
Q2. 一篇关于校内游泳选手在校运会上赢得三面金牌的报道。
A. Swimmer Wins Three Golds at School Sports Day
B. A Student Did Very Well in the Swimming Race
C. The School Sports Day Was Held Last Week
A现在时 Wins ✅、含关键词 Three Golds / Sports Day、简洁 7 词。B 弱动词 Did Well + 无具体信息；C 偏活动介绍而非赛事亮点。
Q3. 一篇关于校际辩论赛中我校辩论队获胜的报道。
A. Debating Team Wins Inter-School Final
B. The Debating Team Has Won the Inter-School Final
C. A Great Win for Our School's Debaters
A现在时 Wins ✅、简洁 4 词、含关键词。B 时态错误（Has Won 过去时）；C 偏评价而非概括事件。
Q4. 一篇关于学校开放日吸引500个家庭参加的报道。哪条标题动词最强？
A. School Open Day Draws 500 Families
B. Many Families Visited the School on Open Day
C. Our School Held a Very Successful Open Day Event
ADraws 强力动词 ✅、现在时、含数字关键词 500。B 用 Visited 弱动词+过去时；C 模糊修饰（very successful）。

1. capture the reader's _______________
2. be _______________, concise and interesting
3. contain _______________ from the article
4. give the reader a sense of what the _______________ is about
答案 1. attention　2. descriptive（或 short / informative）　3. keywords　4. story

Lead = 导语：用 5W1H 概括新闻
阅读以下 lead：
On a Sunday afternoon, 200 people finished a Spartan race at Peak Park. Covered in mud, they climbed over mud pits, a 10-foot wall and monkey bars to reach the finishing line.
📝 Section 2A：找出 5W1H 要素（3分）
Who → ________ | What → ________ | Where → ________
When → ________ | How → ________
答案 Who = 200 people | What = crossed the finishing line of a Spartan race | Where = Peak Park | When = On a quiet Sunday afternoon | How = climbed over obstacles (mud pits, wall, monkey bars)
📝 Section 2B：判断对错（3分）
1. [T/F] A lead should be very long.
2. [T/F] A lead should answer 5W1H questions.
3. [T/F] A good lead should have a strong opening.
答案 1. F — lead 应该 short（短）　2. T　3. T
讲解 · 5W1H 详解
讲解 · Phase 2
Lead 的核心：5W1H
Who — 谁参与了事件
What — 发生了什么
Where — 在哪里发生
When — 什么时候发生
Why — 为什么发生
How — 怎么发生的
💡 好的 lead 不需要包含全部 6 个 W，但至少覆盖 Who / What / When / Where 中的 3-4 个
讲解 · 好导语准则
讲解 · Phase 2
好 Lead 的 4 条准则
① 简短精练
👆 翻牌
Be short and simple
2-3 句为佳
不堆砌细节
抓核心信息
② 回答 5W1H
👆 翻牌
Answer 5W1H
至少覆盖 Who/What/When/Where
Why 和 How 可选
③ 吸引眼球
👆 翻牌
Strong opening
用场景/感官描写开头
例如：On a quiet Sunday afternoon...
④ 主动语态
👆 翻牌
Use active voice（主动语态）
✅ 200 people crossed the line
❌ The line was crossed by 200 people
练习 · 中译英 Lead
练习 · Phase 3 · 中译英
中译英：把以下中文写成英文 Lead（导语）
在一个周日下午，200人完成了在太平山公园举行的斯巴达障碍赛。
💡 词伙提示：周日下午 Sunday afternoon | 200人 200 people | 完成 finished / completed | 斯巴达障碍赛 Spartan obstacle race | 举行的 held at
On a Sunday afternoon, 200 people finished a Spartan race at Peak Park.
我校篮球队在上周六的校际决赛中击败对手，赢得冠军。
💡 词伙提示：击败对手 beat opponents | 校际决赛 Inter-school Final | 赢得冠军 win the championship | 上周六 last Saturday
Our school basketball team beat their opponents and won the Inter-school Final last Saturday.
浑身是泥的参赛者们爬过了泥坑、3米高墙和吊环障碍，才到达终点。
💡 词伙提示：浑身是泥 covered in mud | 爬过 climbed over / crawled through | 泥坑 mud pits | 3米高墙 3-metre wall | 吊环 monkey bars | 终点 finishing line
Covered in mud, they climbed over mud pits, a 10-foot wall and monkey bars to reach the finishing line.
讲解 · Speech 演讲结构
讲解 · Phase 2
Speech：学校集会演讲稿
Speech 的基本结构？
👆 翻牌
Speech 结构 = 4 部分
1. Greeting — 开场问候
2. Introduction — 介绍自己/背景
3. Body — 核心内容 + 经历亮点
4. Closing — 感悟 + 致谢
📌 结构完整是得分基础！
语气和要点？
👆 翻牌
Tone & Key Rules
• 语气：formal 或 semi-formal
• 必须有 greeting（开头）+ closing（结尾）
• 必须有 title
• 不能太 casual / 口语化
📌 学校正式场合 ≠ 和朋友闲聊！
讲解 · Speech 各部分排列
讲解 · Phase 2
Speech 四段结构：按正确顺序排列
演讲稿有严格的结构顺序，缺少或颠倒任何一段都会扣分。
👇 以 e-sports tournament（电竞比赛）为例，按正确顺序点击以下 4 个部分
Body（亮点）
Greeting（问候）
Closing（感悟）
Introduction（背景）
练习 · 中译英 Speech
练习 · Phase 3 · 中译英
中译英：Speech 演讲稿关键句式
各位老师、各位同学，早上好。今天我想分享我组织电竞比赛的经历。
💡 词伙提示：各位老师同学 fellow teachers and students | 早上好 good morning | 分享 share | 经历 experience | 组织 organize / host
Good morning, fellow students and teachers. Today I want to share my experience of organizing an e-sports tournament.
这次经历让我明白了团队合作的重要性。
💡 词伙提示：这次经历 this experience | 让我明白了 taught me / made me realise | 团队合作 teamwork | 重要性 importance
This experience has taught me the importance of teamwork.
我从没想过一个游戏社团能组织这么大的活动。
💡 词伙提示：从没想过 never thought / never imagined | 游戏社团 gaming club | 组织 organize / pull off | 这么大的活动 such a big event
I never thought that a gaming club could organize such a big event.
感谢大家的聆听。希望我的分享能鼓励更多同学尝试新事物。
💡 词伙提示：感谢聆听 thank you for listening | 分享 sharing / speech | 鼓励 encourage / inspire | 尝试新事物 try new things | 同学 fellow students
Thank you for listening. I hope my sharing can encourage more students to try new things.
讲义 · Section 3 Speech
练习 · Phase 3
📋
Section 3：Speech 演讲结构 (18分)
独立完成以下题目
阅读题目，独立作答
题目场景：You are a member of your school Video Gaming Club. You organized your school's first e-sports tournament. Now you are giving a speech at the school assembly about the experience.
📝 Section 3A：排序题（4分）
将以下各部分按 1-4 排序：
___ Talk about the best parts of organizing the tournament
___ Formal greeting
___ Explain what you learnt from this experience
___ Explain how you got involved
答案 1 Formal greeting → 2 Explain how you got involved → 3 Talk about highlights from organizing → 4 Explain what the experience has meant to you
📝 Section 3B：填空 + 判断（6分）
Speech 的语气应为 ________ 或 ________。
开头必须有 ________，结尾必须有 closing。
[T/F] A speech must include a title.
[T/F] The speech should explain why it was meaningful.
答案 语气 = formal 或 semi-formal | 开头必须有 greeting | Title = T | Meaningful = T
📝 Section 3C：Speech 片段分析（4分 · 2题）
Q1. 阅读以下 speech 开头：
"So yeah, we just played some games and it was cool. That's all I wanted to say."
请写出 至少 2 个 这段 speech 的问题：
① ________________________________________
② ________________________________________
参考 ① 语气太随意（"So yeah" / "it was cool" — 太口语化，不适合学校场合）
② 结构缺失：没有 Greeting、没有 Introduction、没有 Closing
（③ 可加分：没有具体内容，没说经历的意义）
Q2. 阅读以下 speech 结尾：
"I'd like to thank everyone for listening. Goodbye."
这段 speech 结尾缺少了什么关键要素？
→ ________________________________________
参考 缺少 Reflection / 感悟 — speech 的 closing 除了致谢，还应该说说你从经历中学到了什么
📝 Section 3D：应用写作（4分 · 2题）
💡 场景：你要在周会上分享组织慈善义卖 (charity sale) 的经历
Q3. 请写一个 speech 的 Greeting（问候）：
→ ________________________________________
参考 Good morning, fellow students and teachers. Today I want to share my experience of organizing our school's charity sale.
评分：Greeting ✓ 自我介绍 ✓ 话题引入 ✓ Formal/semi-formal 语气 ✓
Q4. 请写一个 speech 的 Closing（结尾，含感悟+致谢）：
→ ________________________________________
参考 This experience has taught me the importance of teamwork. Thank you for listening.
评分：感悟 ✓ 致谢 ✓ 正式语气 ✓
讲解 · Rule of Three
讲解 · Phase 2
Rule of Three：三个并列元素增强说服力
将三个相关的词、短语或句子并列使用，形成节奏感和强调效果。
reuse 重复利用
recycle 回收
reduce 减少
更多 Rule of Three 范例：
• "This phone is perfect — in design, in price and in quality."
• "The race tested our strength, courage and teamwork."
📌 三元素：同词性 · 同结构 · 层层递进
讲解 · Repetition
讲解 · Phase 2
Write Like a Pro：Repetition
Repetition 是什么？
👆 点击翻牌
重复 = 刻意重复关键短语来强调信息
定义：重复使用同一个词或句式，强化情感和记忆点。
范例：
• "I trained every morning. I trained every evening. I trained until I couldn't stand."
• "Like other athletes, we train hard. Like other athletes, we never give up."
📌 关键：重复的是句式结构，不是简单复读！
练习 · 中译英 修辞
练习 · Phase 3 · 中译英
中译英：用 Rule of Three 或 Repetition 翻译
这款手机在哪方面都好——好看、好用、便宜。（Rule of Three）
💡 词伙提示：完美 perfect | 好看 looks / design | 好用 speed / performance | 便宜 price / value | 三并列 A, B and C
This phone is perfect — in looks, in speed and in price.
为了保护地球，我们都应该减少使用、重复使用和回收利用。（Rule of Three）
💡 词伙提示：保护地球 protect the earth | 减少 reduce | 重复使用 reuse | 回收利用 recycle | 三并列 A, B and C
To protect the earth, we should all reduce, reuse and recycle.
我每天早上练习。我每天晚上练习。我练习到站不起来。（Repetition）
💡 词伙提示：练习 trained / practised | 每天早上 every morning | 每天晚上 every evening | 站不起来 could not stand | 重复句式 repetition
I trained every morning. I trained every evening. I trained until I couldn't stand.
斯巴达赛考验了我们的力量、勇气和团队精神。（Rule of Three）
💡 词伙提示：考验 test | 力量 strength | 勇气 courage | 团队精神 teamwork | 三元素并列 three qualities
The Spartan race tested our strength, our courage, and our teamwork.
讲义 · Section 4 修辞
练习 · Phase 3
📋
Section 4：修辞手法 (6分)
独立完成以下题目
📝 Section 4A：判断以下句子使用了哪种修辞手法（Rule of Three / Repetition）
Q1. "I trained every morning. I trained every evening. I trained until I couldn't stand." → _______
Repetition — 重复 "I trained" 三次
Q2. "This phone is perfect — in looks, in speed and in price." → _______
Rule of Three — 三个 in + 名词并列
Q3. "To protect the earth, we should all reduce, reuse and recycle." → _______
Rule of Three — 三个动词并列
📝 Section 4B：完成 Rule of Three 句子
The Spartan race tested our _______, our _______, and our _______.
参考 The Spartan race tested our strength, our courage, and our teamwork.
（其他合理答案亦可：speed / skill / patience / willpower）
讲解 · 写作中的常见错误
讲解 · Phase 2
Headline / Lead / Speech 常见错误
Headline 常见错误
👆 翻牌看 3 类错误
① 时态错误
❌ Storm Forced Schools to Close（过去时❌）
✅ Storm Forces Schools to Close（现在时✅）
→ 标题必须用现在时！
② 动词太弱
❌ Basketball Team Did Well in Final（弱动词❌）
✅ Basketball Team Storms to Victory（强力动词✅）
③ 过长 / 缺关键词
❌ A Very Interesting Event Happened at School（太模糊❌）
✅ Robotics Team Wins Top Prize（含关键词✅）
Lead / Speech 常见错误
👆 翻牌看 3 类错误
④ Lead 缺 5W1H
❌ "There was a race. It was fun."
✅ "200 people crossed the line of a Spartan race at Peak Park on Sunday."
⑤ Speech 结构不完整
❌ 无 Greeting（问候）→ 直接讲内容
❌ 无 Closing（结尾）→ 突然结束
❌ 无 Title（标题）→ 丢格式分
⑥ Speech 语气错误
❌ "So yeah, we played games." → 太随意
✅ 学校集会需要 formal（正式）/ semi-formal
练习 · 改错 Headline & Lead
练习 · Phase 3 · 改错
改错练习：找出问题并写出正确版本
💡 每一题都有一个明显错误（时态 / 动词 / 语气 / 结构）→ 先找出问题，再写出正确版本
❌ 标题："Storm Forced All Schools to Close Last Monday"
💡 提示：时态 tense现在时 present tense
错误：用了过去时 Forced
改正：Storm Closes All Schools Across City
（标题必须用现在时）
❌ 标题："Our School Basketball Team Did Very Well in a Match"
💡 提示：弱动词 weak verb缺关键词 keywords
错误：弱动词"Did Well" + 缺具体结果
改正：Basketball Team Storms to Championship Victory
（用强力动词 + 含比赛类型关键词）
❌ Lead："There was a race at the park. Many people came. It was interesting."
💡 提示：缺 5W1H句子太短太简单
错误：缺 Who/How 信息，句子太短太简单，"interesting" 不具体
改正：On a Sunday afternoon, 200 people finished a Spartan race at Peak Park, covered in mud after climbing over mud pits and a 10-foot wall.
（包含 Who/When/Where/How + 具体描写吸引读者）
❌ Speech 开头："Hey guys, I'm gonna talk about the tournament we did. It was pretty fun."
💡 提示：语气太随意 too casual缺 greeting
错误：语气太 casual（Hey guys/gonna/pretty fun）+ 缺 formal greeting
改正：Good morning, fellow students and teachers. Today I would like to share with you my experience of organizing our school's first e-sports tournament.
（Formal greeting + 正式句式 + 话题引入）
讲义 · Section 5 改错
练习 · Phase 3
📋
Section 5：改错 — Headline / Lead / Speech (12分)
独立完成以下题目
📝 Section 5A：改 Headline 错误（4分 · 2题）
💡 检查：时态对吗？动词够强吗？5-10词吗？
#错误标题改正
1Storm Forced All Schools to Shut Down Last Tuesday_______________
时态错误（过去时） Storm Forces City-Wide School Shutdown 或 All Schools Close After Storm
#错误标题改正
2Our School Did Something Good in the Competition_______________
弱动词 + 模糊（不具体） School Wins Top Prize in Inter-School Contest 或 School Takes First Place in Contest
📝 Section 5B：改 Lead 错误（4分 · 2题）
💡 检查：包含 3+ 个 5W1H 吗？吸引读者吗？2-3句吗？
#错误 Lead改正
3There was a basketball game. Our school played. We won._______________
缺 5W1H + 句式单调 Our school basketball team stormed to victory in the inter-school championship final last Saturday, defeating their opponents 78–65 at the Hong Kong Coliseum in front of over 2,000 cheering fans.
#错误 Lead改正
4Last week, something very exciting happened at our school gym._______________
模糊笼统、无具体信息 Last Saturday, our school gym erupted in cheers as the basketball team claimed the inter-school championship title with a thrilling 78–65 victory over their long-time rivals.
📝 Section 5C：改 Speech 错误（4分 · 2题）
💡 检查：有 Greeting 吗？语气够正式吗？有 Closing 吗？
#错误 Speech 片段改正
5"So basically we ran a charity sale. Thanks for coming. Bye!"_______________
语气太随意 + 缺结构 Good morning, fellow students and teachers. I am happy to share with you my experience of organising our school's charity sale. [body] This experience has taught me the importance of teamwork. Thank you for listening.
#错误 Speech 片段改正
6"Good morning, everyone. I'm going to talk about a basketball game. That's all."_______________
缺 Closing + 无感悟 Good morning, everyone. I'm going to talk about a basketball game that changed how I think about teamwork. [body] This experience showed me that success comes from hard work and trusting your teammates. Thank you for your attention.
讲义 · Section 6 短文写作
练习 · Phase 3
📋
Section 6：短文写作 (5分) — 综合运用
独立完成以下题目
信息：你校篮球队在上周六的全港校际篮球决赛中击败对手，获得冠军。队长陈大文 (Chan Tai-man) 得了 28 分，成为最佳球员 (MVP)。比赛在学校体育馆举行，有超过 500 名观众观看。
📝 Task A (2分)：为这篇报道写一个 headline（5-10词）
参考答案
• Chan's 28 Points Lead Team to Basketball Title
• Basketball Team Wins Championship in Exciting Final
• School Wins Inter-School Basketball Final
评分：简洁 ✓ 现在时 ✓ 含关键词 ✓ 得 2 分
📝 Task B (3分)：为这篇报道写一个 lead（2-3句）
Sample Lead
Our school basketball team won the Inter-school Basketball Final last Saturday, beating their opponents at the school sports hall. Team captain Chan Tai-man scored 28 points and was named MVP in front of over 500 cheering fans.
评分：≥3个5W1H要素 ✓ 具体信息 ✓ 主动语态 ✓ 得 3 分
💡 提示：用现在时 + 强力动词 + 关键词（Chan / 28 points / Basketball / MVP）
总结 · 综合应用
总结 · Phase 4
综合应用：找错 · 改错 · 选择
用今天学到的知识，快速判断以下题目
1找出以下 headline 的两个错误：
"A Very Exciting Chess Game Was Held at Our School"
两个错误
① 过去时 "Was Held" → 标题必须用现在时（Holds / Hosts）
② "Very Exciting" 太模糊（不具体） → 应用强力动词 + 关键词（如 Student, 15, Wins Chess Game）
2以下哪条 lead 更好？为什么？
A Last week something exciting happened at our school.
B Over 300 students filled the school hall last Friday to watch the debating team win the inter-school final.
B
A 的问题：太模糊（"something exciting"），没有 5W1H 信息
B 的优势：覆盖 Who(300 students) / When(last Friday) / Where(school hall) / What(win final)，主动语态 + 具体信息
3以下 speech 片段有两个结构问题，请找出：
"I want to talk about the volunteer work we did. We cleaned the beach. It was meaningful. Thanks."
两个结构问题
① 缺少 Greeting — 演讲稿必须以正式问候开头（Good morning, fellow students and teachers.）
② Closing 太简略 — "Thanks" 不是合格的结尾，需要包含感悟（what you learnt from it）+ 正式致谢
4判断以下句子使用了哪种修辞？
a) "We must work hard, work smart, and work together." → _______
b) "We will not give up. We will not back down. We will not stop until we succeed." → _______
答案
a) Rule of Three — 三个短语并列（hard / smart / together），同结构层层递进
b) Repetition — "We will not" 重复三次开头，强调不屈决心
5用今天学到的公式，为以下信息写一条 headline：
你校辩论队在周六的校际决赛中击败对手，第一次赢得冠军。
Headline = 强力动词 + 关键词 + 现在时
参考
• Debating Team Beats Rivals to Win First Title
• Debate Team Wins First Championship
评分要点：现在时 ✓ 强力动词(Beats/Wins) ✓ 关键词(Debating/Title) ✓ 5-9词 ✓
出门测试
出门测试 · Phase 4
出门测试：6 道综合检测
每题请先自己作答，再点击"核对答案"查看解析
Q1以下哪项不是好 headline 的 MUST？
A. 抓住注意 (Capture attention) B. 简洁 + 有信息 (Short & informative) C. 用过去时 (Use past tense) D. 含关键词 (Contain keywords)
C 不是 MUST。好标题永远用现在时（Present Tense），不用过去时。即使事件已过去，标题也用现在时。
Q2好 Lead 应该符合以下哪条？
A. 越长越好 B. 必须用被动语态 C. 简短、回答 5W1H、用主动语态 D. 不需要吸引读者
C 好 Lead 必须简短（2-3 句）、回答 5W1H、使用主动语态和强力动词。
Q3填空：Speech 的四个结构部分依次是：Greeting → _______ → Body → _______
A. Title → Summary B. Introduction → Closing C. Opening → Question D. Body → Title
B Speech 标准结构：Greeting → Introduction → Body → Closing。Introduction 引入主题，Closing 总结反思。
Q4找出错误：以下哪句存在中式英语 / 语法错误？
A. In my opinion, e-sports is good for students. B. According to my opinion, e-sports is very good for students. C. I think e-sports can help students work together. D. In my view, gaming has many benefits.
B 错误！不能说 "According to my opinion"，正确说法是 "In my opinion"。另外 "very good" 太模糊，应改为具体词如 "helpful" 或 "useful"。
Q5判断修辞手法：以下句子使用了什么修辞？
"I trained every morning. I trained every evening. I trained until I couldn't stand."
A. Rule of Three B. Repetition C. Simile（比喻） D. Metaphor（暗喻）
B Repetition（重复）。"I trained" 重复三次开头 → 制造强烈节奏感 + 强调训练之刻苦。与 Rule of Three 的区别：Repetition 是重复同一个句式，Rule of Three 是三个不同元素并列。
Q6应用：为以下新闻写一条英文 headline
你校游泳队在上周五的校际游泳比赛中获得 5 面金牌。
请先自己作答，然后点击下方按钮查看参考
Swim Team Wins 5 Golds at Inter-School Meet
评分标准：现在时 "Wins" ✓ | 强力动词 ✓ | 关键词 5 Golds / Inter-School ✓ | 简洁 7 词 ✓
Writing skill builder · Noun clauses · Usage

A noun clause is a group of words that functions as a noun. We can use noun clauses:

Usage 用法Example 例句中文释义
as the subject of a sentence
作句子主语		That she was unhappy is not surprising.她不开心这件事并不令人意外。
as the object of a sentence
作句子宾语		I haven't decided which subjects I will study.我还没决定要修哪些科目。
after a preposition
置于介词后		We had an argument about where we should go on holiday.我们为去哪儿度假争吵了一番。
after the verb to be
置于 be 动词后		The question is whether they will accept our offer.问题是他们会不会接受我们的提议。
after certain abstract nouns
置于抽象名词后		I've just heard a rumour that Steven is moving to Tokyo.我刚听到传闻说 Steven 要搬去东京。
after it + be + adj. / present participle
it + be + 形容词/现在分词 后		It was uncertain whether he would be picked for the team. It's disappointing that he hasn't made more of an effort.他能否入选队伍还不确定。/ 他没更努力让人失望。
after subject + be + adj. / past participle
主语 + be + 形容词/过去分词 后		She is happy that she has so many close friends.她很高兴有这么多亲密的朋友。
after it + be/seem + a/an + noun
it + be/seem + 名词 后		It's a pity that we won't be able to meet up.很遗憾我们无法见面。
after it + appear/happen/seem/turn out
it + 发生类动词 后		It appears that we'll be going to London after all.看来我们终究要去伦敦了。
Writing skill builder · Noun clauses · 辨析与注意

名词性从句 和 定语从句 可互换

📘 名词性从句 Noun Clause

I am surprised by what he did.

他的所作所为让我惊讶。 what he did = the things that he did

📙 关系从句 Relative Clause

I am surprised by the things that he did.

他做的那些事让我惊讶。 that he did 修饰 the things

⚠️ 注意：从句中的主语始终在动词之前

❌ 错误 (Wrong)

Could you tell me what time is it now?

在名词性从句中错误地使用了疑问句倒装语序

✅ 正确 (Correct)

Could you tell me what time it is now?

从句中主语 (it) 在动词 (is) 之前 —— 只有直接疑问句才倒装

对比直接疑问句：'What time is it?' she asked. ← 直接疑问句才倒装

Writing skill builder · Why use noun clauses?

1️⃣ Make the article clearer and easier to understand

📝
Parents want their kids to be perfect is natural.
→ That parents want their kids to be perfect is natural. / It is natural that parents want their kids to be perfect.

2️⃣ Explain difficult concepts

📝
When you want to say "很多老一辈人依然重男轻女" and you don't know how to translate "重男轻女" in English, explain it with a noun clause:
"Many old people still hold the traditional belief that males are more valuable and important than females."

3️⃣ Add variety to the sentence structures used

📝
Are you attending certain events next year? Have you decided yet?
→ Dear Miss So, Have you decided what event you are attending next year?

Then I began to wonder (7) ＿＿＿ students would be more keen to read if the books they could choose from were popular with their peers. The answer was a definite "yes". Peer influence is very important to teens, despite (8) ＿＿＿＿ we are talking about reading,' Charlotte explains.

The next thing that you may be wondering is (9) ＿＿ the bookcrossing corner will work. It has been decided (10) ＿＿ anybody will be able to borrow a book. (11) ＿＿ you should return the book doesn't matter. There is no deadline and no overdue fine for that. Just relax and enjoy reading!'

If you support Choi's idea, just bring some of your favourite books to the corner. 'As the area is just opening, it is pretty empty. An initial stock of donated books is (12) ＿＿ is needed to get the ball rolling, so please give generously,' Charlotte says. Lastly, remember (14) ＿＿ the bookcrossing corner is open—from 12 pm to 1 pm daily. You are all welcome to share and read books at that time!

Writing skill builder · Reported speech · commonly tested in DSE Paper 1 & 3

When we change direct speech (i.e. the exact words someone says) to indirect, or reported, speech, we often need to change:

直接引语 Direct Speech间接引语 Reported Speech
verb tenses'I'm exhausted,' said Paul. 'I was in the gym. I've been working out for hours.'Paul said (that) he was exhausted. He explained that he had been in the gym and that he had been working out for hours.
modal verbs'We must accept the offer,' said Sue. 'We may not get another one.'Sue told me (that) we had to accept the offer as we might not get another one.
subject and object pronouns'I need to speak to you,' said Dan.Dan told me (that) he needed to speak to me.
possessive adjectives and pronouns'My kite is the blue one,' Simon reminded me. 'Yours is green.'Simon reminded me that his kite was the blue one and that mine was green.
demonstrative adjectives and pronouns'This project is driving me crazy!' exclaimed Peter. 'These are your books,' said Will.Peter exclaimed that the project was driving him crazy. Will said (that) those were my books.
expressions of time and place'I have been here since yesterday,' said Tim. 'I'm leaving tonight.'Tim said (that) he'd been there since the day before/the previous day and (that) he was leaving that night.
word order*'Who is Ron meeting?' asked Mum. 'Are you going with him?'Mum asked who Ron was meeting and whether/if I was going with him.
reporting verbs†'You should go to bed,' said Tina.Tina advised/urged me to go to bed. Tina suggested that I (should) go to bed.

*When reporting questions.   †When reporting requests, commands, advice, etc. Note that we use different patterns with different verbs.

Writing skill builder · Reported speech · Special cases & Writing focus

特殊情况 Special Cases:

  • verbs in the past simple tense → past perfect or do not change (when there is an expression of definite past time, e.g. in 1989)
  • verbs in the past perfect → do not change
  • modal verbs could, might, ought to, should, would, had better and would rather → do not change
  • must → had to (for obligations)
  • When we report facts or habitual actions, we can use the same tense the speaker uses (if things have not changed).

✍️ 写作应用 Writing Focus

We can use reported speech to communicate the things that someone has said. We often use it in:

  • survey or research reports
  • news reports

Reported questions · word order changes

In reported speech, we need to make changes to the original word order. These changes include:

1. Introductory verbs

In reported questions, we use the introductory verbs ask, wonder, want to know, try to find out, etc. instead of say, tell, etc.

2. Other points to remember:

  • In reported questions, the word order is subject + verb.
  • If a direct question begins with a question word (who, what, how, etc.), the question word is kept in the reported question.
  • If it is a yes/no question, we normally use if or whether.
